why: The c1 blank is decodable and unforced. 'that drive skeletal muscle' visible IS the definition of a motor neuron, so a non-knower reads the answer off the stem (check 15 crutch); and several answers fit the hole equally (motor neurons / motor nerves / efferent neurons), so it is not one-answer. This is a location fact, not a term-to-meaning definition, so parker-preferences' two-way default does not apply (lists, sequences, numbers and location facts stay single-direction). Parker's own margin note on this highlight asked for exactly one fact here: 'motor neuron cell bodies reside in the spinal cord.' Kept that direction, dropped the decodable naming direction.
revised_Text: The cell bodies of the motor neurons that drive skeletal muscle reside in the {{c1::spinal cord::structure}}.

why: Hint leak. '::nerve fiber' is a synonym for the hidden answer 'axon' - the card's own Back Extra says 'an axon is the long fiber a neuron extends...', so the hint could replace the answer and mean the same thing (check 9's exact test; check 20's 'hint restates the answer's meaning' clause). Removed it. The stem 'extends an ___ out to a skeletal muscle' already forces axon (dendrites do not run to muscle), and the Meaning line in Back Extra still closes the prerequisite after he answers.
revised_Text: A motor neuron extends an {{c1::axon}} out to a skeletal muscle, and an impulse generated by the {{c2::cerebral cortex}} travels down it to make that muscle {{c3::contract}}.

why: Hint leak plus an open blank underneath it. '::PNS nerve type' expands to 'peripheral nervous system nerve type', which hands over the answer word 'peripheral' (check 9). The same hint is legitimate on card 113 because 'cranial' is not inside it - here it is not. And once the leaking hint is removed, the blank is no longer forced: 'A ___ runs from the brain through the spinal cord to a body part' also admits spinal nerve / somatic nerve, so it fails cold-solve. Fix: make 'peripheral nerve' the visible anchor and test the two facts Table 6-10 actually teaches for that row - the brain to spinal cord to body part routing, and the bidirectional traffic. Both blanks stay anchored, so no husk.
revised_Text: A peripheral nerve runs from the brain through the {{c1::spinal cord}} to a body part, so it both {{c2::receives stimulus from the body}} and {{c2::sends commands to the body}}.

why: Ungrounded and factually wrong framing. 'Of the two epidermal layers' is not in the source and contradicts it: p614 says 'Epidermal cells are arranged in multiple layers', and card 115 in this same batch says new cells 'ascend through the other skin layers'. Replaced the frame with a grounded one. The forced-choice binary hints and the germinal-vs-corneum contrast are untouched - the visible entity anchors make this the multi-dimensional contrast R10 clears, not a husk.
revised_Text: Within the epidermis, the germinal layer {{c1::is::is or is not}} supplied with blood, while the stratum corneum {{c1::is not::is or is not}}.

why: Etymological leak in BOTH directions - the R3 class the brief flagged. The c1 card hides 'Sebaceous glands' while 'secrete sebum' stays visible (sebum gives you sebaceous); the c2 card hides 'sebum' while 'Sebaceous glands' stays visible. Either blank is decodable by a student who knows no skin anatomy at all. This is not the protected two-way definition shape - the two spans are a gland and its secretion, not term and meaning. Fix: put both names under one cloze number so neither can be read off the other. The visible remainder (lie next to the hair follicles, an oily substance that travels along the follicle to the skin surface) is a substantial forcing anchor, so this is not a husk, and the connective is not an identity connective so R10b does not apply.
revised_Text: {{c1::Sebaceous glands}} lie next to the hair follicles and secrete {{c1::sebum}}, an oily substance that travels along the follicle to reach the skin surface.

why: The R3 leak the brief predicted, found. 'retroperitoneal' was hidden while its own literal meaning - 'lie behind the abdominal cavity' - stayed VISIBLE on every card the note generates and was never itself clozed. Retro- plus peritoneum IS 'behind the abdominal cavity', so a non-knower decodes the term (check 15), and the meaning rode along as untested scenery (check 4). R3's must-not-over-flag protection covers a two-way definition where BOTH halves are clozed under different numbers; here the meaning half was never clozed at all, so the protection did not apply. Fix per R3/R4: give the meaning its own cloze number, which converts the card into the protected two-way definition and re-tests the moved fact instead of dumping it in Back Extra. The organ pair and the rib-to-vertebra span keep their own numbers so nothing that was tested is lost. Digits verified verbatim against p623: '11th rib to the third lumbar vertebra'.
revised_Text: The {{c1::kidneys and pancreas}} are called {{c2::retroperitoneal::classification}} organs because they lie {{c3::behind the abdominal cavity}}, above the level of the umbilicus and extending from the {{c4::11th rib to the third lumbar vertebra::span}} on each side.

why: The 98% blank is arithmetic, not recall. On the c2 card the stem still reads 'saliva is approximately ___ water, with the remaining 2% made of...', so anyone who can subtract from 100 produces the answer without knowing anything about saliva. Fix: put the two complementary figures under the SAME cloze number so neither gives away the other. The c2 card then reads 'approximately ___ water, with the remaining ___ made of mucus, salts, and organic compounds' - both forced for a knower, and the composition list anchors the stem so it is not a husk. Digits verified verbatim against p625: 'nearly 1.5 L of saliva daily. Saliva is approximately 98% water. The remaining 2% is composed of mucus, salts, and organic compounds.'
revised_Text: The salivary glands produce nearly {{c1::1.5 L}} of saliva daily, and saliva is approximately {{c2::98%}} water, with the remaining {{c2::2%}} made of {{c3::mucus}}, {{c3::salts}}, and {{c3::organic compounds}}.
